occupancy_signal_status.note: citation_occupancy is WITHHELD. NOT SEPARATED: the known-open and known-closed controls measured the same. The instrument cannot tell the two known classes apart, so it is not measuring openness on this channel. known_open=0, known_closed=0, required margin 0.1. Every probe therefore carries citation_occupancy: null, scripts/atlas/build_query_atlas.mjs records winnability_basis "unmeasured_neutral" for every query, and scripts/queries/join_atlas_to_release_queue.mjs admits no candidate on this signal. The observation is NOT withheld: cited_hosts_in_order, host_classification and every bucket share are recorded in full and are re-derivable with --rescore-only. What is refused is publishing a winnability number the controls say is not measuring winnability.
occupancy_signal_status.what_this_channel_shows: Across 209 queries and 1878 citation slots, 6 slot(s) are held by nothing durable. On the answer-engine citation channel a slot is held by an incumbent service provider, by an institution, or by a host we cannot identify - and none of those are ground a new page takes by finding them empty. "Who currently holds the slot" is therefore not a measure of whether a page can win it, which is what this metric was being read as.
occupancy_signal_status.what_would_lift_it: Either a control pair whose two classes are known to differ ON THIS CHANNEL (the current priors were taken on Bing SERP top-10, a different population, which the file already records as comparable_to_prior: false), or a winnability measure that is not "is the slot empty" - for example whether this portfolio has been observed taking a slot from the class of holder that occupies it.

admission_rules.why_required: The atlas ranks unmeasured rows with a neutral factor so ordering is not distorted by a number nobody took. Ranking is not admission: a query may only become a page candidate once its citation occupancy has actually been measured. This is the gate that replaced the hardcoded 0.5 weak_incumbent_score, which admitted and blocked nothing.
admission_rules.minimum_citation_occupancy_why: unbranded_share is the fraction of answer-engine citation slots an independent page could plausibly take. Below this, the slots are held by national brands, social surfaces or our own pages, and a new page is competing for something that is not open.
admission_rules.maximum_candidates_per_run_why: A processing budget, never a publication quota. The same principle page_strategy_registry.json states for daily cadence.
admission_rules.near_duplicate_jaccard_why: page_strategy_registry.json states that a wording variation is not a distinct page intent, but the release queue only compares routes and titles, so two orderings of the same words pass it as two pages. Candidates whose content-word sets overlap at or above this threshold collapse to the higher-ranked one and the loser is held naming the query it duplicates. 0.8 keeps a qualifier that changes the answer (0.75) as its own page.
admission_rules.demand_evidence_exempt_tiers_why: T3 is defined in evidence_queries.json as 'real phrasing, no volume': a query observed verbatim in an agent run against a live answer engine, for which no volume figure exists. No volume figure CAN exist - this portfolio has no paid keyword source, and the one file a previous pass cited for it was found never to have existed. Requiring demand evidence of T3 therefore did not hold pages to a higher standard, it made a whole tier permanently unpublishable while query_atlas.json's own policy said 'pages may only be generated against evidence_tier T1-T3' and validate_query_atlas.js explicitly exempted T3 from the demand requirement. Two governing files disagreed and this one silently won. This records the resolution instead of leaving the contradiction in place.
admission_rules.minimum_citation_occupancy_for_demand_ex: A demand-exempt tier clears a higher winnability bar than the 0.3 base floor. Stated honestly: this does NOT substitute for demand evidence, because citation occupancy and search volume measure different things - a query nobody searches can still show a high unbranded share. What actually bounds the risk is that publication is itself the demand test here: the release cadence is 2 new URLs/day and maximum_candidates_per_run is 5, so an unwanted query costs one page and is observable, and ingest_gsc_evidence promotes a T3 row to T1 with superseded_tier as soon as Search Console measures it. The higher floor is a proportionate hedge, not a proof of demand.

ranked_by: measured citation occupancy (unbranded share of answer-engine citation slots), then atlas rank_score within band
stop_reason: occupancy_signal_withheld:CONTROL_PAIR_DOES_NOT_SEPARATE - data/signals/query_class_occupancy.json is refusing to publish citation_occupancy because its control pair does not separate, so no query has an admissible winnability reading and this lane admits nothing. This is a measurement failure, not a missing run: re-running npm run probe:occupancy will withhold again. Either a control pair whose two classes are known to differ ON THIS CHANNEL (the current priors were taken on Bing SERP top-10, a different population, which the file already records as comparable_to_prior: false), or a winnability measure that is not "is the slot empty" - for example whether this portfolio has been observed taking a slot from the class of holder that occupies it.
